title: Red Horse Chestnut: Ancient Chestnuts You Can Visit
meta_description: A hybrid bred for pink flowers, not conkers. Amersfoort's, from the 1880s, stands between the medieval tower and the old pig market square.
intro: The red horse chestnut is a cross bred deliberately, joining the white-flowered chestnut of every European avenue with a red-flowered American buckeye, first recorded in Germany around 1820. The result flowers pink in May instead of white, sets almost no spiny conkers, and largely escapes the leaf miner moth that browns out its white parent by late summer. It was planted for gardens, not found in the wild, which shows in where the old ones stand. Amersfoort's, from the 1880s, grows between the Onze Lieve Vrouwetoren and the old Varkensmarkt. In Leeuwarden one survived the redevelopment of a former hospital garden with crown anchors and a trunk wound to show for it. The one on the Wilhelminaplein has nothing written down about it at all, and in the Bronx family tradition says a Van Cortlandt planted the one on the lawn of their 1748 house.
